transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. Well, I'm mostly here because... I just can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations at work. Again and again. I do bookkeeping for this plumbing supply place, and honestly, the office is freezing. Like, they keep the AC blasting even though it's barely sixty degrees outside, and I bought this little space heater for under my desk, but the building manager said it was a fire hazard. Which is ridiculous because it has an auto-shutoff feature. I made sure of that when I got it at Target. They had a really good sale in the home goods aisle... 

But, um, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, the spreadsheets. Yeah, I end up staying at work for hours after everyone else leaves. Just sitting there in the cold, checking the math even when I already checked it and I know I checked it. Because... if I don't do it just one more time, I get this horrible feeling that something really bad is going to happen, and it'll be completely my fault. So I just stay and keep checking.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks a specific number of times?

A specific number? Um... not exactly a number, I guess. It's more like I just have to keep going back over the calculations again and again. I mean, sometimes I try to tell myself I'll just check it three times. Three is my lucky number. Actually, I was the third child in my family, and my mom always said the third time's the charm. She used to bake these amazing three-layer cakes for our birthdays, with the real buttercream frosting? Not the fondant kind. I hate fondant, it honestly just tastes like sweet plastic. I watched this baking show the other day where they made a whole life-sized dog sculpture out of fondant and I just thought, nobody is actually going to eat that. It's a total waste of sugar and food coloring. 

But um, wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, the number of times. Yeah, so I try to stop, but even if I check it three times, or ten times, I still end up staying at work for hours after everyone else is gone. Because even when I *know* I already checked the spreadsheets, I get that awful feeling that if I don't do it just *one more time*, something terrible is going to happen and it'll be my fault. So the number doesn't even matter, I just can't stop going back over them. It's always just... one more time.
Do you think something bad would happen because you made a mistake in the spreadsheets?

Yeah, exactly, it's... it's like this thought that just won't leave me alone. Even after I know the numbers match, this thought keeps jumping in that I missed one hidden mistake in payroll or taxes. And if I did, somebody's check won't go through, or the firm will get in trouble. Which, honestly, my boss is already so stressed out because his wife just had twins, and they're renovating their kitchen at the same time. I don't know why anyone would plan a renovation right when they're having babies. The dust alone would drive me crazy. I helped my dad sand the deck once when I was in high school, and I swear I was coughing up sawdust for a week. We used this cherry wood stain that smelled so strong, it gave me a headache. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the mistakes. Yeah, so I try to push the thought away, like, I tell myself, 'You just looked at this, it's fine.' But it comes right back. It's like I can't even trust my own eyes anymore. I just keep thinking about someone not getting paid and it being all my fault.
Do you feel like the spreadsheets need to be perfect or symmetrical in some way for you to consider them complete?

Um, perfect? Or symmetrical? I mean, I guess I like things to look neat, but it's not really about how they look on the screen. The columns don't have to be exactly the same width or anything. Although, I did spend like twenty minutes last Tuesday trying to get the company logo to center perfectly on this invoice template. The program we use is so old, it's basically from the stone age. It's called QuickBooks, but like, a version from ten years ago. My boss refuses to upgrade because he says it costs too much, but then he just bought this massive espresso machine for the breakroom. Which nobody even knows how to use! It has all these dials and steam wands, and I tried to make a latte once and just ended up spraying hot milk all over my cardigan. It was my favorite one, too, this mustard yellow one I got at a thrift store. I love thrift shopping, you can find such unique stuff. I found this vintage Pyrex bowl set last weekend...

But, sorry, um... what were we talking about? Symmetrical? Right, no, it's not about the layout or making it look perfect like that. It's really just the numbers. I just have to know the numbers are right. It's not a visual thing, it's just that horrible feeling that I missed a mistake.
Do you feel less anxious when you've completed your checks on the spreadsheets?

Less anxious? Um... I guess maybe for a second? Like, right when I hit save and close the window, there's this tiny moment of relief. But it doesn't last. It's almost like... like when you take a sip of water when you're really thirsty, but then the glass is empty and you're still thirsty. I actually bought this huge insulated water bottle recently because I was trying to drink more water. It's one of those ones that holds like, half a gallon, and it has these little motivational quotes printed on the side for every hour? Like, "Keep going!" and "You're almost there!" It's supposed to help you track it. But honestly, it's so heavy when it's full, I feel like I'm doing a bicep curl every time I take a drink. I took it to my cousin's wedding last month because it was an outdoor ceremony and it was so hot. She wore this beautiful lace dress, but I swear she was melting. They had these little paper fans on all the chairs, which was a cute idea, but they didn't really do anything. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the anxiety. Yeah, so the relief just doesn't stay. Because the second I walk away from my desk, or even just look at a different screen, the doubt comes right back. I start thinking, 'Wait, did I actually check that last column, or did I just think I did?' And then my chest gets all tight again, and I just have to go back and open the file one more time. So no, I don't really feel less anxious. It just starts all over again.
Do you feel like you're trying to control something by repeatedly checking the spreadsheets?

Control something? I mean, I guess I'm trying to control the fact that I might have messed up. It's like I have to go back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone leaves, just checking them. It gets so quiet in the office when everyone is gone. It's kind of spooky, actually. The air conditioning turns off at like 6 PM, and then you just hear this weird hum from the vending machine in the hallway. I bought a bag of pretzels from it once, and they were completely stale. Like, rock hard. I think the guy who refills it only comes once a month. My friend Sarah used to work in an office where they had free snacks, like those little bags of trail mix and fresh fruit. She said she gained like ten pounds her first year there just from eating the free snacks. She's doing this keto diet now, though, where you eat a lot of cheese and meat. I don't think I could do that, I love bread too much. I went to this bakery last weekend and got a sourdough loaf that was still warm... 

But um, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, controlling things. Yeah, I just... I can't stop checking them. Even when I know I already checked them, I have to do it one more time. Because if I don't, I just get this overwhelming feeling that something terrible is going to happen, like I said, and it'll all be my fault. So I guess I'm just trying to control that feeling, or stop the bad thing from happening.
Do you think your need to keep checking the spreadsheets is more about preventing a mistake or making sure everything is in its right place?

Um, it's definitely about preventing a mistake. It's not about things being in the right place, like, I don't care if my desk is messy. My desk is actually a total disaster right now. I have all these sticky notes everywhere. I use the neon pink ones because they stand out, but then I just cover my monitor in them and I can't even see the edges of the screen. I buy them in bulk from this office supply store near my apartment. The guy who works there, Gary, he always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts. Even in the middle of winter! He says he used to live in Florida and he just refuses to adapt to the cold here. I've never been to Florida. I've always wanted to go to Disney World, though. My friend went last year and she said the lines were crazy, like two hours just for one ride. She brought me back these Mickey Mouse ears with little sequins on them, which was sweet, but I don't really know when I'm supposed to wear them. Maybe for Halloween? I usually just dress up as a cat for Halloween because it's easy. Just draw on some whiskers with eyeliner...

But wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, preventing a mistake. Yeah, it's like... even after I know the numbers match, and I've checked them, this thought just keeps jumping into my head. Like, what if I missed one hidden mistake in payroll or the taxes? And then somebody's check won't go through, or the firm will get in massive trouble. I try so hard to push the thought away, like, I tell myself I just looked at it. But it comes right back. It's like I literally can't trust my own eyes.
Is it the possibility of making a mistake that drives you to check the spreadsheets repeatedly?

Yeah, exactly. It's the possibility of that mistake that just... it won't leave me alone. Like I was saying, even after I know the numbers match, this thought just keeps jumping into my head. I'll be sitting there, and suddenly it's like, what if I missed one hidden mistake in the payroll, or the taxes? And then somebody's check won't go through, or the firm is going to get in massive trouble because of me. 

My boss, Mr. Henderson, he's always stressing about the taxes. He drinks so much coffee, I swear he's vibrating by noon. He has this mug that says "World's Okayest Boss" on it, which is pretty funny, but it's stained brown on the inside because he never washes it. Just rinses it out. I read an article once about how many bacteria live on unwashed coffee mugs in offices. It's actually disgusting. They said you're better off using disposable cups, but then that's so bad for the environment. I tried using those bamboo reusable cups for a while, but they make the coffee taste kind of like dirt? Or maybe it was just the brand I bought. I got them on sale at Target. I always end up buying things I don't need at Target. Like last time, I went in for toothpaste and came out with a waffle maker and three throw pillows. The pillows are really soft, though. They're like a mustard yellow color, which I didn't think I'd like, but it actually brightens up my living room a lot...

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. The spreadsheets. Right. So, yeah, it's that thought about the payroll or taxes. I try so hard to push it away, you know? I try to tell myself I just looked at it and it was fine, but it comes right back. It's honestly like I can't even trust my own eyes anymore.
Is it the fear of making a mistake that drives you to check the spreadsheets repeatedly, rather than needing them to be perfect?

Um, yeah, I think... wait, didn't you just ask me that? But yeah, it's definitely the fear of a mistake. Not them being perfect. I don't even know how a spreadsheet could be perfect, really. I mean, unless it's like, color-coded? I do like color-coding things sometimes, just for fun. I actually ordered this set of pastel highlighters online a few weeks ago. The shipping took absolutely forever because they came all the way from Japan. But then the mail carrier left the package out on my porch while it was pouring rain, so the cardboard box got all soggy and literally fell apart when I tried to pick it up. Luckily the highlighters were wrapped in plastic. 

I really like the mint green one. I use it to mark off my grocery lists. I usually try to go to the grocery store on Sunday mornings right when they open because it's way less crowded. If you go on a Sunday afternoon, it's just packed with people blocking the aisles with their carts, and everyone is moving so slow. There's this one lady who always gives out samples of cheese in the deli section, and she wears this little hairnet that kind of looks like a spiderweb. I always feel bad taking a sample and not buying the cheese, but it's usually like eight dollars for a tiny block of it, and I just can't afford that on my salary...

Oh, gosh, sorry. I'm rambling again. What did you ask? Right, perfect. Yeah, to answer your question, it's not about perfection at all. It's just... I'm terrified I made a mistake, like I was saying.
Do you feel like checking the spreadsheets repeatedly helps you feel more in control of your work?

Um, I don't know if it makes me feel in control. Maybe the opposite? Because I don't really want to be doing it. It just feels like I have to. Like if I don't, something terrible is going to happen. 

Speaking of terrible things happening, my sister called me last night in a total panic because her cat, Barnaby, got out. He's this huge, fluffy Maine Coon, and he's strictly an indoor cat. He's actually kind of a scaredy-cat, honestly. He hides under the bed whenever the doorbell rings. I bought him this little bowtie collar for Christmas, it's plaid, and he looked so handsome in it, but he managed to wriggle out of it in like five minutes. Anyway, she left the front door open for just a second while she was bringing in groceries, and he bolted. She was out walking the neighborhood with a flashlight for like three hours. She said the mosquitoes were awful. I hate mosquitoes. I always get those huge welts when they bite me, and they itch for days. I tried that trick where you put clear nail polish over the bite to stop the itching, but it just made my skin peel off and it looked really gross...

Wait, sorry. Did I answer your question? You asked about control, right? Yeah, I don't think I feel in control at all. I don't really know what it makes me feel, just... stuck, I guess. Like I have to do it.
Do you feel like checking the spreadsheets is a way for you to avoid feeling responsible for a potential mistake?

Um, avoiding feeling responsible? I'm not really sure about that. I mean, it's my job, so I *am* responsible for it, you know? I don't think checking it over and over changes that fact. I just really, really don't want to be the one who ruins everything. 

Speaking of being responsible for things, they actually put me in charge of ordering the birthday cake for Sarah in HR last week. She's gluten-free, which is totally fine, but the bakery I usually go to on 4th Street doesn't do gluten-free, so I had to drive all the way across town to this specialty bakery. The traffic was just unbelievable. There was this huge pothole on the interstate that everyone was swerving to avoid, and the guy in front of me had this bumper sticker that said "Tell your dog I said hi." I love dogs so much. I really want a Golden Retriever, but my apartment building has a strict no-pets policy. They don't even let you have fish tanks over ten gallons because apparently someone's tank broke a few years ago and flooded the unit below them. Water damage is so awful. My parents had a pipe burst in their basement when I was in middle school, and it ruined all these old family photo albums. My mom tried to dry them out with a hair dryer, but the pages all stuck together...

Oh, gosh, I'm doing it again. I'm so sorry, my brain just keeps wandering today. Um, but yeah, to answer your question... I don't think it's about avoiding responsibility. I just don't want there to be a mistake at all.
Do you feel like you're trying to achieve a sense of certainty by checking the spreadsheets repeatedly?

Um, certainty? I guess... I mean, I don't really know if I ever feel certain. It's more like I'm just trying to make the bad feeling go away for a second, but it never really lasts. So I wouldn't say I actually get to feel certain about anything. 

It's kind of like when you check the weather app, you know? Like, it says there's a zero percent chance of rain, but then you look outside and the clouds are super dark. I actually got caught in a huge downpour last Tuesday when I was walking to my car after work. I had just bought these really cute suede boots, too, they were on clearance at this little boutique downtown. The girl working there was so nice, she actually threw in a free pair of fuzzy socks because it was my first time shopping there. They're pink with little white polka dots. I love fuzzy socks, especially in the winter when my apartment gets drafty. The heating in my building is so weird, it's either freezing cold or boiling hot. Last winter, the radiator in my bedroom started making this awful clanking noise at like three in the morning, and the maintenance guy said it was just air trapped in the pipes. He had to bleed the radiator, which sounded like a medical procedure, honestly. I hate going to the doctor... well, not you, obviously, but like, regular doctors. The waiting rooms always smell like rubbing alcohol and old magazines...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being certain about the spreadsheets. Um, yeah, no, I don't think I ever actually feel certain. I just... I don't know, I just keep checking because I can't stop.
Do you feel like the spreadsheets or your work needs to be organized in a specific way for you to feel comfortable?

Um, organized in a specific way? I don't... I don't really think so. I mean, they're just spreadsheets, you know? They just have rows and columns like they always do. I don't really care how they look or anything like that. It's just the numbers I'm worried about.

Speaking of numbers, I was trying to balance my own checkbook the other day, which I know is so old-school, right? Nobody uses checks anymore. But my landlord still requires a physical check for rent, which is just so annoying. I have to buy stamps just for him. The post office was totally out of the regular flag stamps last time I went, so I had to buy these ones with different types of frogs on them. They're actually kind of cute, but the guy at the counter was so slow. He just kept talking to the lady in front of me about his grandson's baseball game. I guess the kid hit a home run or something, which is great, but I was on my lunch break and I just wanted to get my stamps and leave. I always get the turkey sandwich from the deli next door on my break. They use this really amazing cranberry mayo, it's so good. I tried making it at home once, but I used too much cranberry sauce and it just tasted like Thanksgiving dessert on a sandwich. I love Thanksgiving, though. My aunt always makes this sweet potato casserole with the little marshmallows on top...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? You asked about the spreadsheets being organized. Um, yeah, no, I don't really need them to be organized a certain way. It's not about that. I just... I just don't want to mess up.
Do you feel like the spreadsheets need to be organized or laid out in a specific way for you to feel okay about them?

Um, organized in a specific way? No, I don't think so. I mean, they're just normal spreadsheets, you know? Like I was saying, it's really just the numbers I'm worried about, not how they look. 

I actually really hate trying to make things look pretty on the computer. Like, my boss asked me to make a flyer for the office holiday party last year, and it took me hours. I couldn't figure out how to get the little snowflake clip art to line up right. I ended up just using a template I found online, but it printed out all weird because our office printer is ancient. It always jams if you put more than ten sheets of paper in the tray. The IT guy, Kevin, he comes down to fix it at least twice a week. He's always wearing these really loud Hawaiian shirts, even in December. I asked him where he gets them once, and he said he buys them in bulk from this website that sells vintage clothes. I love vintage clothes, actually. I found this amazing 1950s swing dress at a thrift store last month, but it was like two sizes too small. I bought it anyway because the pattern was just these gorgeous little yellow daisies. Daisies are my favorite flower. My grandma used to grow them in her garden, along with these huge sunflowers that were taller than I was when I was a kid. We used to roast the sunflower seeds in the oven with salt...

Oh, my gosh, I'm so sorry. I totally lost track again. Um, but no, the spreadsheets don't need to be laid out a certain way. I just... I just have to check the numbers.
Do you feel like the spreadsheets need to be symmetrical or have a certain order for you to consider them complete?

Symmetrical? Um, no. I mean, no, not really. It's really just the numbers. I don't care if the columns are even or whatever. As long as the math is right, that's all that matters. 

Math was actually my worst subject in high school, which is so funny since I'm a bookkeeping clerk now. I had this teacher, Mr. Henderson, and he always smelled like old coffee and peppermints. He used to make us do these pop quizzes on the overhead projector. Do you remember those? The ones with the clear plastic sheets and the markers that always got all over your hands? I got a blue marker stain on my favorite sweater once. It was this really soft cashmere cardigan my mom got me for my birthday. She always buys me clothes that are just a little too preppy for my style, but I wear them anyway because she tries so hard. She actually just started taking this pottery class at the community center, and she made me this bowl that's supposed to be for cereal, but it's like... the size of a mixing bowl. I use it to hold my keys and mail by the front door instead. I get so much junk mail, it's ridiculous. Mostly credit card offers and those coupons for the local pizza place. The pizza there is actually pretty good, though, they have this garlic knot crust...

Sorry. Sorry! I'm rambling again. Um, no, the spreadsheets don't need to be symmetrical or anything. I just... I just can't stop checking if the numbers are right.
Do you think your repeated checking of the spreadsheets is more about being in control or avoiding mistakes?

Oh, avoiding mistakes. Definitely avoiding mistakes. I mean, I'm literally here because I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. I'll stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves, even when I've already checked them. 

The office gets so spooky when it's empty, too. The air conditioning shuts off at like 6 PM on the dot, so it gets really stuffy, and the security guard, Gary, always does his rounds right at 7. Gary is super nice, he always brings in donuts on Fridays from this little bakery near his house. They have these maple bacon donuts that are incredible. I didn't think I'd like bacon on a donut, you know? It sounds kind of gross, mixing meat with pastry, but the salty and sweet combination is just so good. I actually tried to make candied bacon at home once after having one of those donuts, but I burned it to an absolute crisp and set off the smoke alarm in my apartment. My cat, Barnaby, was terrified. He hid under the sofa for like two whole days, and I had to coax him out with little pieces of tuna. Tuna is the only wet food he'll eat, he's so picky. I tried giving him the salmon pate once and he literally tried to bury it like it was in his litter box...

Oh my gosh, I'm doing it again. I am so, so sorry. My brain just goes a mile a minute. What was I saying? Um... right, staying late with the spreadsheets. I just... even if I know I checked them, if I don't do it just one more time, I get this overwhelming feeling that something really bad is going to happen, and it'll be entirely my fault.
Do you think your repeated checking is more about making sure everything is perfect or about fearing that you've made a mistake?

It's definitely the fear of making a mistake. It's not about them being perfect, it's... it's this terrifying thought that I messed up. Like, even after I *know* the numbers match, and I've added up the columns three times, this thought just keeps jumping into my head that I missed one hidden mistake somewhere in payroll or the taxes. And if I miss it, somebody's paycheck won't go through, or the firm will get in huge trouble with the IRS, and it'll all be my fault. I try so hard to push the thought away, but it just comes right back. It's like I literally can't trust my own eyes anymore. 

Speaking of eyes, I actually just had to go to the optometrist last week because I broke my glasses. I sat on them! Can you believe that? I left them on the passenger seat of my car when I ran into the grocery store, and when I got back in, I just completely forgot they were there. *Crunch*. The frames were completely bent out of shape. They were these really cute tortoiseshell ones, too. I got them at this little boutique downtown that sells independent designer frames. The girl who works there, Chloe, she has the most amazing hair. It's dyed this vibrant, almost neon pink, and she always styles it in these intricate braids. I tried to braid my hair like that once after watching a YouTube tutorial, but my hair is just too fine. It always slips right out of the hair ties. My mom has really thick, curly hair, and I've always been so jealous of it. She uses this special shampoo that smells like coconuts and mangoes, it makes the whole house smell like a tropical vacation whenever she showers. We actually went to Hawaii for a family vacation when I was in middle school, and we went snorkeling... 

Oh, no. I'm so sorry. I did it again, didn't I? I just... I start talking and I can't stop. But yeah, it's the fear of a mistake. The thoughts just won't leave me alone, no matter how many times I check.
